messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Metoprolol crosses the placenta and passes into breast milk in small amounts.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding.
Studies published to date have not shown a link between metoprolol taken in pregnancy and major birth defects or miscarriage.
Reports on growth restriction, early birth, and death around the time of birth have been inconsistent.
Those studies have limitations that make studies hard to interpret.
Untreated high blood pressure and untreated heart failure in pregnancy carry their own serious risks for both mother and baby.
Babies born to mothers taking metoprolol may have low blood pressure, low blood sugar, a slow heartbeat, or slow breathing.
Babies born to mothers taking metoprolol are watched after birth.
The amount of metoprolol a breastfed baby receives is estimated at 0.05 mg to under 1 mg a day.
This amount is about 0.5% to 2% of the mother's weight-adjusted dose.
No side effects in breastfed babies have been identified.
Babies are still monitored for a slow heartbeat and for signs such as unusual sleepiness.
Triplet: ["Metoprolol", "may cause in baby", "slow heartbeat"]

The relation 'may cause in baby' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug may lead to the adverse effect or condition specified by the object entity in the baby.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has side effect': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
B. 'has pregnancy or breastfeeding warning': The subject drug carries the warning specified by the object entity regarding use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
C. 'has side effect frequency': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect specified by the object entity with the frequency indicated.
D. 'has serious side effect': The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
E. 'has side effect more likely in': The subject drug is more likely to cause the specified adverse effect or reaction in the population or group specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.
